messages.author: cd5305fc32b5381b
messages.subject: radial chart in ggplot2
parts:
Hi,

I'm attempting to reproduce a 'radial traffic analysis' chart (http://
www.infovis-wiki.net/images/5/59/Rta_small.jpg) in ggplot2. I have
produced an ordered data.frame object like the simplified version
below:

> traffic.df
value type
display count
1 location1 location
location1 1000
2 location1_org1 organisation organisation1
700
3 location1_org2 organisation organisation2
300
4 location1_org1_100.1.1.1 address 100.1.1.1 300
5 location1_org1_100.1.1.2 address 100.1.1.2 400
6 location1_org2_100.1.2.1 address 100.1.2.1 300
7 location1_org1_100.1.1.1_25 port 25
100
8 location1_org1_100.1.1.1_80 port 80
200
9 location1_org1_100.1.1.2_80 port 80
400
10 location1_org2_100.1.2.1_80 port 80
300

If I run the following on the first 6 rows of the data (i.e. not the
port data), I get something similar to the chart I want:

> p <- ggplot(cut.traffic.df, aes(type, count, fill=display))
> p + geom_bar(position="fill") + coord_polar(theta="y")

However, when I run this on the full data frame I get the following:

> p + geom_bar(position="fill") + coord_polar(theta="y")
Error in if (!all(data$ymin == 0)) warning("Filling not well defined
when ymin != 0") :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I've established that this has something to do with the 'display'
column containing repeated values (i.e. "80") and have tried setting
'fill=value' which draws the chart but does not colour the port bar
consistently (i.e. I would like all occurences of 'port 80' to be the
same colour).

If anyone has a suggestion as to how to solve this (or start again
from scratch) I'd be really happy to hear.

Thanks,
Joe

> file=trafficAnalysis.R"></script>

[Incorporating the gist inline:]

traffic.df <- structure(list(value = structure(c(1L, 2L, 8L, 3L, 6L, 9L,
4L,
5L, 7L, 10L), .Label = c("location1", "location1_org1",
"location1_org1_100.1.1.1",
"location1_org1_100.1.1.1_25", "location1_org1_100.1.1.1_80",
"location1_org1_100.1.1.2", "location1_org1_100.1.1.2_80",
"location1_org2",
"location1_org2_100.1.2.1", "location1_org2_100.1.2.1_80"), class =
"factor"),
type = c("location", "organisation", "organisation", "address",
"address", "address", "port", "port", "port", "port"), display =
c("location1",
"organisation1", "organisation2", "100.1.1.1", "100.1.1.2",
"100.1.2.1", "25", "80", "80", "80"), count = c(1000, 700,
300, 300, 400, 300, 100, 200, 400, 300)), .Names = c("value",
"type", "display", "count"), row.names = c(NA, -10L), class = "data.frame")
p <- ggplot(traffic.df, aes(type, count, fill=display))
p + geom_bar(position="fill") + coord_polar(theta="y")

geom_bar by default summarizes the data. In this case, your data is
pre-summarized. So you need stat="identity"

p + geom_bar(position="fill",stat="identity") + coord_polar(theta="y")
